title: Introduce histogram resampler and epoch condenser for compact latency summaries
author: Lina Chen
release_notes: Add a histogram resampler and epoch condenser to compress per-epoch telemetry while preserving tail fidelity; no runtime API changes; opt-in via config; reduces payload size for long-running benchmarks.
body:
Motivation: Our long-running benchmark reports accumulate high-cardinality per-epoch histograms which make nightly archives large and slow to analyze. This PR adds a lightweight histogram resampler plus an "epoch condenser" that compresses sequential epoch histograms into a compact representation for downstream reporting while preserving p95/p99 fidelity and reconstruction accuracy for investigative dives.

Design: The histogram resampler converts dense per-epoch histograms into a two-stage representation: a compact coarse histogram for fast queries and a delta sketch that captures tail shifts between epochs. The epoch condenser groups epochs into configurable windows (default 8) and emits a single condensed record with metadata for reconstructing approximate epoch-level tails. Both components are implemented as streaming operators in the benchmark reporter pipeline to avoid memory spikes.

Key properties: 1) Tunable fidelity vs compression via `compress_ratio` and `tail_sensitivity` settings. 2) Online-friendly: constant memory per running group. 3) Deterministic merge semantics for multi-run aggregation.

Usage: Opt-in by setting `reporter.condense.enabled=true` and tuning `reporter.condense.window_size` and `reporter.resampler.tail_sensitivity`. Backwards-compatible: when disabled the reporter emits the legacy per-epoch histograms unchanged.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for resampler math and deterministic merges added; end-to-end pipeline test verifies that condensed reports reconstruct p95/p99 within 1.5% on the internal stable workload corpus. Perf harness runs (attached below) show 6-12x reduction in stored histogram bytes for high-resolution runs with <0.8% additional CPU overhead on the reporter process.

Checklist: * [x] Design doc linked in linear (ENG-4321) * [x] Unit + integration tests * [x] Performance regression run completed * [x] Backwards compat opt-out * [x] Docs and example config added

Related: This PR is the follow-on to the preforked-kvcache telemetry reductions (ENG-4187) and is intended to reduce noise when running 24h suffix stability sweeps.

Tomás: 'Please add metrics for condenser throughput and bytes-saved.' Author: 'Added condenser.metrics.bytes_saved and condenser.metrics.epochs_collapsed in last commit.' perf_results_summary: Condensed-report runs on stable corpus: payload bytes reduced from 96MB -> 12MB for 24h high-res sweep (8x), p95 reconstructed error median 0.6%, p99 error 1.2%, reporter CPU increase median 0.4%, max observed 0.8%. Storage/ingest downstream query times improved ~30% on aggregated dashboards.
notes_for_future_work: Follow-ups: 1) Add adaptive window sizing based on workload drift (ENG-4389). 2) Explore lossy compression of delta sketches for ultra-long-term archives. 3) Expose knob to route condensed vs raw to different archival buckets.
